correctness.rationale: Finite-dimensional dissipativity isolates the reducing hub-nodal eigenmode subspace. Dirichlet path modes have unique reduced rational frequency labels; a single weighted hub constraint determines each eigenspace. Exact orthogonal projection and primitive-residue trigonometric summation give the rational survival formula, and strict positivity yields the lcm node test. All quantifiers and boundaries B>=3, lengths>=1, positive J,gamma and 1<=d<=L_i were checked. Independent full-adjacency eigenspace computations passed 321 small graphs and 2904 source probabilities; they corroborate rather than replace the proof.

originality.rationale: An exact arithmetic, site-resolved strong-limit absorption law is not stated or implied by the inspected sources: the 2022 equal-arm same-topology article uses rotational symmetry and optimizes detuning-dependent absorption times, the 2020 paper uses branched peripheral stars, and the 2017 dark-state paper states a general projector principle but no unequal-arm divisor-sum evaluation. Published mathematical-result searches for the precise formula and its structural aliases returned no stronger covering theorem; closest published results concern different combinatorial or continuum spectral invariants. This is a best-knowledge, not independently certified, priority assessment.
residual_risks: Preexisting equivalent arithmetic statement under other spectral-graph or physical terminology remains possible; negative searches alone do not establish novelty.

value.rationale: A natural full classification of the dark-space dimension and *site-resolved* exact capture probabilities for arbitrary asymmetric multiarm chains directly addresses how geometry and injection position change absorption efficiency. The arithmetic node criterion predicts certain sites perfectly absorb even when other dark modes exist. This structural, reproducible design rule goes beyond the known symmetric-arm reduction and generic spectral projector framework; no external theorem or paper-size contribution is required.
